question: g4_orders_list
answer:
Created [src/util/ordersApi.mjs](~/code/benchmark/okf-local/main/no_okf/work/g4_orders_list/no_okf/codex/5/src/util/ordersApi.mjs) exporting `normalizeOrderList(response)`, no imports. It maps:

- `orders` ← `response.orders` (else `[]`)
- `pages` ← `response.totalPages` (else 0)
- `total` ← `response.recordsTotal` (else 0)
- `onThisPage` ← `response.recordsOnThisPage` (else 0)

Verified with Node: a full response normalizes to `{orders:[1,2], pages:3, total:17, onThisPage:5}` and a missing/undefined response yields `[]`/`0` defaults. Only that file was added; nothing else changed.

Files used to determine the shape:
- [src/pages/other/RecentOrder.js](~/code/benchmark/okf-local/main/no_okf/work/g4_orders_list/no_okf/codex/5/src/pages/other/RecentOrder.js) — the page that loads the order list; shows the payload is used directly as `response.orders` and references `response.totalPages`.
- [src/pages/category/Category.js](~/code/benchmark/okf-local/main/no_okf/work/g4_orders_list/no_okf/codex/5/src/pages/category/Category.js) — same backend's list response, confirming the field names `totalPages` (pages) and `recordsTotal` (total records).
- [src/util/webService.js](~/code/benchmark/okf-local/main/no_okf/work/g4_orders_list/no_okf/codex/5/src/util/webService.js) — confirms the "response" the pages receive is the raw JSON body (`response.data`), so the function reads body fields directly.

One caveat: the repo never reads a "records on this page" field for orders, so `recordsOnThisPage` is inferred from the backend's `recordsTotal` naming convention — the one field I couldn't confirm against code.
